entities.text: ORAL JUDGMENT S R Raval - Food Inspector vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Judgment and order dated 28.02.2011 rendered by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No.8, Ahmedabad, recording acquittal for the respondent for the offences punishable R/CR.A/835/2011 JUDGMENT under Sections 7(1) and 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (for short "the Act") in Criminal Case No.27 of 2002 has been assailed in this Appeal under Section 378(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for short Cr.P.C.).

2. The only ground urged for assailing the judgment and order is that in absence of respondent no.2 rendering a positive evidence establishing the purchase of the packed food article namely coriander powder with warranty from its manufacturer, distributor or dealer, the benefit of warranty under Section 19(2) of the Act was not available to him.

3. As against that the submission made by the learned counsel for the respondent is that the food article in question was a packaged food article labelled with the complete name and address of the manufacturer clearly indicating that the burden to show that the first respondent was the purchaser of the food article manufactured by its manufacturer was discharged.
It is also contended that in absence of the manufacturer and dealer being arraigned as accused, the first respondent could not have been prosecuted.

The learned counsel has placed reliance upon State of Gujarat Vs.
Manishbhai Narandas Karia [2007 (1) FAC Pg.96].
4.

entities.text:
State of Gujarat Vs.
Manishbhai Narandas Karia [2007 (1) FAC Pg.96]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having considered the rival contentions, to this Court it appears that the case is squarely covered by the said pronouncement.

Like in the said case, in the present case also concededly, the food article was a packaged food article labelled with the complete name and address of the manufacturer, and infact, the letters addressed by the Food Inspector to manufacturer though received, were not responded to by it.

In all the relevant R/CR.A/835/2011 JUDGMENT documents produced on record namely, report of the Public Analyst - Exh.-2, which mentions "Coriander (Dhania) Powder (Gurukrupa Brand Company Pack)", Exh.-3 - details of sample as indicated by the public analyst, Form - VI issued under Rule 12, which mentions in Gujarati "manufactured by - Gurukrupa Sales Corporation, near Gokalpura Bus-stand, Manjipura Road, Nadiad, Post-Dabhan, Pin- 387320", acknowledgment receipt issued by Local Health Authority containing similar description, justify the undisputed fact that the respondent was not the manufacturer and full details in relation to the manufacturer were disclosed on the label of the packaged food article itself.
Infact, Prosecution Witness-1 has admitted the fact that Gurukrupa Sales Corporation as the manufacturer of the food article in question, has been referred to in various documents.
Thus the burden under Section 19(2) of the Act as interpreted by this Court in State of Gujarat Vs. Manishbhai Narandas Karia (Supra) stood discharged, in this case as well.

entities.text: State of Gujarat Vs. Manishbhai Narandas Karia
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. For the foregoing reasons, no substance is found in this Appeal against acquittal.
Accordingly, the Appeal fails and is dismissed.

(G.R.UDHWANI, J.) Dolly S R Raval - Food Inspector vs State Of Gujarat on 3 May, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191460599/
